name: Coloured bathroom suite
summary: A bath, a basin and a WC glazed in the same strong colour: pink, green, blue, yellow or later avocado. The even gloss glaze and the matching set make the bathroom a room of colour.

philosophy.core_thesis: Sanitary ware can be a colour of the room, and one even glaze on every piece makes a bathroom that matches.
design_principles: Glaze the basin, the pan, the cistern and the bath in one colour from the same batch.
Choose one pastel or earth colour: pink, sky blue, mint, buttercup yellow or avocado green.
Shape each piece with soft curves and a radius of 30 to 60 mm on every edge.
Keep the glaze even, with a gloss of 85 to 95 GU and no pattern.
Match the colour of the tiles, the towels and the walls to the suite.
Add chrome taps with a small white or clear cross handle.
Mould a shell, a ridge or a streamline band as the only relief.
anti_patterns: A white suite with a coloured bath only
Two different shades of one colour in a set
A printed flower pattern on the glaze
A dark matte glaze that stains
A thin shape with a sharp edge

form.shape: A set of a pedestal basin, a close-coupled WC, a bidet and a bath with a panel, all with round, soft shapes.
form.profile: Smooth, full curves with a streamlined swell at the front of the basin and a low, wide cistern on the pan.
form.foot_and_rim: A rolled, thick rim with a soft radius, a pedestal that follows the line of the bowl, and a flat base.
form.proportion: Basin 560 to 650 mm wide, 3 to 4 tap holes with a chrome mixer; wall 8 to 14 mm; bath 1700 mm long.
rules: Use one colour for all pieces of a set.
Round every edge and corner, so that there is no hard line.
Keep the form of each piece in line with the next piece.
Let the glaze be the only decoration.

bodies.rule: Use a dense white vitreous body, so that a thin coloured glaze looks clean and does not stain. The colour sits in the glaze, not in the body.

forming.joins: The pedestal and the basin are separate casts; the cistern and the pan are bolted with rubber seals and chrome fittings.
forming.details: A moulded maker name on the back, a clean glaze line at the foot, and a slight tone change at a thick corner.

glaze.pattern: No pattern. A plain colour covers each piece, and the only relief is a shell, a rib or a streamline band.
glaze.gloss: High gloss, about 85 to 95 GU, even over the whole surface.
glaze.wear: The colour fades in the sun, a grey mark appears at the plug and the tap, and a thin glaze crazes with age.

palette.strategy: One strong or soft colour for the whole suite, from pink and mint to avocado, with chrome as a bright accent.

firing.kiln: A gas or oil tunnel kiln, with one long glost firing.
processes: check the colour against a tile
firing.scale: An industrial works; each colour needs its own batch so that a whole set matches.
firing.signs: A thin tone change at thick corners, a stilt mark under the foot and a number of the batch on the back.

pieces.form: Pedestal basin in pink with a soft rim and 3 tap holes
Close-coupled WC in mint green with a low, wide cistern
Panel bath in sky blue with a rolled rim
Low cistern with a streamline band in buttercup yellow

evidence.title: Pink bathroom suite, Skaill House, Orkney

emotion.target_response: A bright, tidy cheer: the viewer sees a bathroom as a place of colour, and thinks of a clean, new house.

use_cases: a film set for a 1950s house
a retro bathroom brief with matching tiles
avoid_when: the brief wants a white minimal bathroom
the brief wants Victorian print and relief

modifiers.how: Change the glaze to white, make the bowl a tight rectangle and hang it on the wall.
Change the glaze to white, add a transfer print and a moulded rim.

wall_thickness.note: The wall of a vitreous basin is thinner than the wall of a fireclay bath.
